s0.why: Sentence 1 defines it as a linear shaped lowland between highlands or mountain ranges produced by a geologic rift; long and straight paraphrases linear.

s1.why: 2 gives the pulling apart of the lithosphere, 3 the deepening by erosion, 4 the filling with sediment from the flanks and surroundings.

s2.why: 9 places the most extensive rift valley on the mid-ocean ridge crest; 20 and 21 say many of the largest lakes, Baikal included, lie in rift valleys.

f0.why: 9 says the most extensive rift valley is along the crest of the mid-ocean ridge system.

f1.why: 11 lists the East African Rift, Rio Grande rift and Baikal Rift Zone as the three currently active.

f2.why: 21 puts Baikal in an active rift valley and 22 calls it the deepest lake in the world.

f3.why: 22 states Baikal has 20% of all the liquid freshwater on earth.

f4.why: 28 gives the 4,000 km long Valles Marineris on Mars as believed by planetary geologists to be a large rift system.

q1.why: 2 says rifts form from pulling apart of the lithosphere and 1 says a rift produces a linear lowland between highlands.

q2.why: 22 gives the 20% figure and says Baikal is both deepest and greatest in volume.

q3.why: 13 says continental rifts that continue eventually become oceanic rifts; 12 covers plates breaking apart.

q4.why: 9 locates the most extensive rift valley on the mid-ocean ridge crest as a result of sea floor spreading.

q5.why: 15 says extension occurs when the bend is in the same direction as the fault motion; 16 adds stretching and subsidence.
